title: fix(data-objectstack): a console page load reads sys_user_preference once, shared by the three preference adapters (objectui#12187)
body:
Fixes #12187

Clause-②: no

This is item 3 of objectui#12187, and the last one: one `sys_user_preference` read per console load. Items 1 (`54159d3`) and 2 (`6eca5b5`) landed earlier, and this PR does not touch their code. Claim `6119197321`, amended for this item by `6122942302`.

## What changes

The change is to `createObjectStackUserStateAdapter` in `@object-ui/data-objectstack` (`userState.ts`). Its `load()` now joins an open read for its data source, resource and user. Every load in that scope that starts before the next microtask adds its key to that read. The read is then sent once, and each adapter takes its own row from the answer.

- **One key in the read:** it sends the same per-key query the adapter has always sent (`user_id = U and key = K`, `$top: 1`).
- **Several keys in the read:** it sends one query, `user_id = U and key in (K1, K2, K3)`, with `$top` set to the number of keys.
- **Nothing is cached.** The read closes as soon as it is sent. A later `load()` asks the server again, and a different user or data source never joins another one's read.
- **`save()` is unchanged.** A write still finds and writes its own row: a per-key find, then an update or an insert.
- **Out of scope, untouched:** the server, the stored rows and the row shape.

`ConsoleShell.tsx` does not change. Its `UserStateBridge` already builds the three adapters in one effect, so the providers' loads land in one read. No reader makes a read of its own, so no reader file changes.

**Published surface:**
- `index.ts` is unchanged.
- `userState.ts` has the same `export` lines as at the base (diff exit 0).
- `ObjectStackUserStateAdapterOptions` is the same as at the base (diff exit 0).
- The new functions and the `SharedRead` interface are module-private.
- The only change that reaches `dist/index.d.ts` is one new paragraph of text in the module's header comment, which tsup copies into it.

Hence `Clause-②: no` and a `patch` changeset for `@object-ui/data-objectstack`. `@object-ui/app-shell` only changes a test.

## H1: the reads per load, before and after

**How it was measured:** a jsdom boot of the real `ConsoleShell` providers and the real `ConnectedShell` over a counting global `fetch`. The shell includes the real `AdapterProvider`, `ObjectStackAdapter`, client and `UserStateBridge`. Two entries were booted: `/apps/demo/page/welcome`, and `/` with a metadata-gated redirect to that page. Only the session is stood in. The call sites come from a sync stack read at `ObjectStackAdapter.find`. The probe was a scratch file and is not committed. The committed pin is `consoleUserPreferenceBudget.test.tsx` (see Tests).

**Before:** at base `adfbe3b` (`main`, which contains `6eca5b5`). Each entry made 3 GETs, each filtered by one key, not by the user's whole set:

| # | request (both entries) | call site |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `GET /api/v1/data/sys_user_preference?top=1&filter=["and",["user_id","=","u1"],["key","=","ui.flow.palette.recents"]]` | `FlowPaletteRecentsProvider` hydrate effect, then `adapter.load()`, `findExisting`, `ObjectStackAdapter.find` |
| 2 | same, `["key","=","ui.recent"]` | `RecentItemsProvider` hydrate effect, same chain |
| 3 | same, `["key","=","ui.favorites"]` | `FavoritesProvider` hydrate effect, same chain |

**After:** at this head, each entry made 1 GET:

`GET /api/v1/data/sys_user_preference?top=3&filter=["and",["user_id","=","u1"],["key","in",["ui.flow.palette.recents","ui.recent","ui.favorites"]]]`

The same three provider effects issue it, now joined into one read.

The `/` entry does not remount `ConnectedShell` on its redirect: the same element type sits at the same position. So it also reads once, before and after.

**Browser reading: NOT MEASURED.** Reason: this container has no runnable backend for a signed-in console. The jsdom boot is the instrument. The staging reading (cloud's pin carrying this merge) is the card's acceptance 3, and it stays with the seat.

## H2: the shape chosen, and why

**Chosen:** the share lives inside `userState.ts`. A module-scope `WeakMap` holds the open reads, keyed by the data-source object and then by (resource, user). This adds no export, option or type.

**Not chosen:** one loader built in `ConsoleShell` and passed to the three adapters. That needs a new option on the factory, which widens the published surface.

**Why `key in` the three keys, and not the user's whole set:**
- The whole set carries every other preference the user has. The object's own description names theme, locale and plugin settings.
- A page cap on that larger set could drop one of the three keys.
- The membership query reads exactly the rows the three per-key reads did. It uses the same `user_id` predicate.
- The object's unique index on (`user_id`, `key`), per organization, allows at most one row per key. So a `$top` equal to the key count drops none.
- The server's filter AST accepts `in`: it is an `AST_OPERATOR_MAP` key behind `VALID_AST_OPERATORS` in `@objectstack/spec`'s `data/filter.zod.ts`, and driver-sql's operator switch has an `in` arm. I read these sources at objectstack `2e11d9006`. No live server was run here.
- objectui already sends `$in` reads through `find` with `$top` equal to the list length (`AccessExplainPanel`).

**A row that carries no `key`:** in an answer for several keys it cannot be assigned to one. When that happens, each adapter reads its own key as before. The pin `a shared answer whose rows name no key is not attributed` covers this.

## H3: refresh and invalidation

**When each adapter reads:**
- No provider re-reads on focus or visibility.
- The hydrate effects in `FavoritesProvider`, `RecentItemsProvider` and `FlowPaletteRecentsProvider` re-run only when the attached adapter or the user id changes.
- The bridge builds new adapters when the user id changes, when the data source changes, or when it remounts under `MetadataProvider key={language}` on a language switch.
- A write reads nothing back.
- Cross-tab sync goes through `localStorage` events only.

**Readings** (same jsdom boot; the "before" column was taken under the ablation below):
- **Account switch, u1 to u2:** before, 6 GETs: 3 for u1 from the outgoing adapters, whose answers the providers' hydration token discards, plus 3 for u2. After, 2 GETs: 1 plus 1. The u2 read asks for u2's three keys, and every consumer ends on u2's rows.
- **A load after the read was sent:** a new request. With one key, it is the per-key query.
- **Writes after boot:** 3 writes, one PATCH to each adapter's own row id, and no extra GET.

## H4

Neither `GET /api/v1/runtime/config` nor `GET /api/v1/auth/me/localization` appears in this boot reading. Their initiators (`index.html` `applyEarlyBranding` and app-shell `initRuntimeConfig`, called from `main.tsx`) are outside the mounted tree, so whether they double is not measured here.

## This reverses an earlier reading

objectui#5544 and objectui#11797 recorded three reads per load as the correct budget ("three different questions"), and their pins held that. objectui#12187 rules the budget at one.

- `consoleUserPreferenceBudget.test.tsx` (the objectui#5544 file) is rewritten.
  - It now boots the real shell instead of a copy of the bridge.
  - It pins one read, and keeps the payload half that objectui#5544 cared about: every consumer still gets its own row.
- `userState.inflightShare-11797.test.ts`: the first case moves to the shared read. The other two cases (one key loaded twice at once is one request; a load after a save reaches the server) are unchanged.

## Tests (at `55be3d7`, through the verify lock)

- **Build:** `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/data-objectstack^...' --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2`: 28 successful. `@object-ui/data-objectstack` was rebuilt at head.
- **Type-check:** `@object-ui/data-objectstack` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit`) and `@object-ui/app-shell` `type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`). Both pass, and both scripts were echoed. `--listFilesOnly` shows that both programs compile the edited tests.
- **Targeted vitest:** every test file that names `createObjectStackUserStateAdapter`, `sys_user_preference` or `UserStateAdapters`, including the new pins: `Test Files 14 passed (14)`, `Tests 161 passed (161)`.
- **The pins:**
  - `consoleUserPreferenceBudget.test.tsx`, five cases: one read per boot asking for the three keys; every consumer gets its own row; each adapter writes only its own row; an account switch reads again for the new user; one key loaded twice at once is one request.
  - `userState.sharedRead-12187.test.ts`, six cases: user scope; nothing kept past the send; data-source scope; untagged rows; a failed read; writes unchanged.
- **Ablation**, with the fix committed first, through objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`:
  - The mutation was `const row = await loadExisting();` to `const row = await findExisting();`, which turns the share off. Anchor 1 to 0, blob `cc27d4d` to `bc3fb25`.
  - Predicted direction: red. Result: 12 failed, 8 passed across the four files. Every count pin fails with three reads where it expects one ("expected … to have a length of 1 but got 3"). The cases that do not depend on the share stayed green: same-key coalescing, user scope, data-source scope, writes.
  - Restore: blob equals HEAD (`cc27d4d`), and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
  - The pins import source through the vitest alias, so no `dist/` is on their resolution path.
- **Gates**, all exit 0: `check:eager-closure` (`Console eager closure is 3126.9 KB gzipped across 70 of 2253 chunks (budget: 3204.6 KB, headroom: 77.6 KB)`, membership exact, on a console `vite build` at head), `check-changeset-presence`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:test-path-roots`, `changeset:check`.
- **ESLint, narrowed and measured:** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 4 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files.
  - Result: 4 files, 0 errors, 1 warning. The warning is the existing `DataSource` typed with `any` on the options member; the base file has the same 1.
  - The `**/*.{ts,tsx}` block of `eslint.config.js` covers all four files.
  - The narrowing excludes nothing: linting is not type-aware (a grep for `projectService|typeChecked|tsconfigRootDir|parserOptions` exits 1), and no `eslint-rules/*.js` reads the filesystem. So the diff cannot change the verdict on an untouched file.
  - The repo-wide `pnpm lint` belongs to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **Pre-existing, unchanged in kind:** on an account switch, the outgoing adapters still make one read for the previous user before the bridge attaches the new ones. The providers discard that answer through their hydration token, so no consumer shows it. The count drops from 3 to 1 with this PR. Nothing is filed: there is no wrong answer to show for it, and no carrier.
- **The share covers only reads in flight.** A bridge remount after the read was sent, such as a language switch, costs one more read. That is a later load, and it has to read afresh.
